stories.title: Kochi: The double-capture race
stories.situation: A Tabby payment could be confirmed by two paths at the same time: the provider's webhook and the app polling for the result. Both could try to capture the same payment.
stories.action: Siwar added an atomic capture claim in MongoDB (findOneAndUpdate on the payment's state), so only one path can claim the capture; the other logs it and skips safely. Refunds got idempotency keys and late webhooks on finished payments are ignored.
stories.result: Only one path can capture a given payment, whichever arrives first; the other skips safely.

stories.title: Kochi: Exchange-rate provider outage
stories.situation: Package prices are shown and charged in SAR, converted from 9 currencies through an external exchange-rate provider. If the provider failed, checkout would break.
stories.action: Siwar built an exchange-rate service with caching: fresh rates are reused, and when the provider fails it falls back to the last cached rate, marks the source as a fallback and logs it. Prices are also frozen into the contract at payment time.
stories.result: Payments keep working during provider outages, and every charge keeps the exact price the client agreed to.

stories.title: Barea: Migrating live curriculum content without breaking it
stories.situation: Barea's curriculum content was stored in a legacy text format and had to be converted into structured blocks while the platform was live in production.
stories.action: Siwar built the converter with a dry-run mode, a comparison step that classifies and explains every difference between old and new content, a safety gate shared by migration, editing and Excel import, review flags for blocks needing a human check, and a rollback script that refuses to write without --confirm-rollback and --backup-confirmed.
stories.result: The migration can be previewed, reviewed and reversed before and after it touches production data.

stories.title: Bawsalah: Making AI-generated reports dependable
stories.situation: Bawsalah generates a career report with an LLM and RAG; model output could break the expected structure or fail transiently.
stories.action: Siwar added validation of the career recommendations against the expected sections and format, counting each rule violation, plus automatic retries capped at 8 attempts that stop early on non-retryable errors, and tracing of RAG responses and generation time.
stories.result: Invalid reports are detected and regenerated instead of being delivered, and failures are visible to the team.
